shortDescription: Modifies query rules using the proxysql admin interface

options.name: OK_msg
options.description: The specified message will be returned for a query that uses the defined rule.

options.name: active
options.description: A rule with I(active) set to C(False) will be tracked in the database, but will be never loaded in the in-memory data structures.

options.name: apply
options.description: Used in combination with I(flagIN) and I(flagOUT) to create chains of rules. Setting apply to True signifies the last rule to be applied.

options.name: cache_empty_result
options.description: Controls if resultset without rows will be cached or not.

options.name: cache_ttl
options.description: The number of milliseconds for which to cache the result of the query. Note in ProxySQL 1.1 I(cache_ttl) was in seconds.

options.name: client_addr
options.description: Match traffic from a specific source.

options.name: comment
options.description: Free form text field, usable for a descriptive comment of the query rule.

options.name: config_file
options.description: Specify a config file from which I(login_user) and I(login_password) are to be read.

options.name: delay
options.description: Number of milliseconds to delay the execution of the query. This is essentially a throttling mechanism and QoS, and allows a way to give priority to queries over others. This value is added to the mysql-default_query_delay global variable that applies to all queries.

options.name: destination_hostgroup
options.description: Route matched queries to this hostgroup. This happens unless there is a started transaction and the logged in user has I(transaction_persistent) set to C(True) (see M(community.proxysql.proxysql_mysql_users)).

options.name: digest
options.description: Match queries with a specific digest, as returned by stats_mysql_query_digest.digest.

options.name: error_msg
options.description: Query will be blocked, and the specified error_msg will be returned to the client.

options.name: flagIN
options.description: Used in combination with I(flagOUT) and I(apply) to create chains of rules.

options.name: flagOUT
options.description: Used in combination with I(flagIN) and apply to create chains of rules. When set, I(flagOUT) signifies the I(flagIN) to be used in the next chain of rules.

options.name: force_delete
options.description: By default we avoid deleting more than one schedule in a single batch, however if you need this behaviour and you are not concerned about the schedules deleted, you can set I(force_delete) to C(True).

options.name: load_to_runtime
options.description: Dynamically load config to runtime memory.

options.name: log
options.description: Query will be logged.

options.name: login_host
options.description: The host used to connect to ProxySQL admin interface.

options.name: login_password
options.description: The password used to authenticate to ProxySQL admin interface.

options.name: login_port
options.description: The port used to connect to ProxySQL admin interface.

options.name: login_unix_socket
options.description: The socket used to connect to ProxySQL admin interface.

options.name: login_user
options.description: The username used to authenticate to ProxySQL admin interface.

options.name: match_digest
options.description: Regular expression that matches the query digest. The dialect of regular expressions used is that of re2 - U(https://github.com/google/re2).

options.name: match_pattern
options.description: Regular expression that matches the query text. The dialect of regular expressions used is that of re2 - U(https://github.com/google/re2).

options.name: mirror_flagOUT
options.description: Enables query mirroring. If set I(mirror_flagOUT) can be used to evaluates the mirrored query against the specified chain of rules.

options.name: mirror_hostgroup
options.description: Enables query mirroring. If set I(mirror_hostgroup) can be used to mirror queries to the same or different hostgroup.

options.name: multiplex
options.description: If C(0), multiplex will be disabled. If C(1), try to enable multiplex. There can be other conditions preventing this (for example, user variables or transactions). If C(2), multiplexing is not disabled for just the current query. By default, does not change multiplexing policies.

options.name: negate_match_pattern
options.description: If I(negate_match_pattern) is set to C(True), only queries not matching the query text will be considered as a match. This acts as a NOT operator in front of the regular expression matching against match_pattern.

options.name: next_query_flagIN
options.description: When is set, its value will become the I(flagIN) value for the next queries.

options.name: proxy_addr
options.description: Match incoming traffic on a specific local IP.

options.name: proxy_port
options.description: Match incoming traffic on a specific local port.

options.name: re_modifiers
options.description: Comma separated list of options to modify the behavior of the RE engine. With C(CASELESS) the match is case insensitive. With C(GLOBAL) the replace is global (replaces all matches and not just the first). For backward compatibility, only C(CASELESS) is the enabled by default.

options.name: replace_pattern
options.description: This is the pattern with which to replace the matched pattern. Note that this is optional, and when omitted, the query processor will only cache, route, or set other parameters without rewriting.

options.name: retries
options.description: The maximum number of times a query needs to be re-executed in case of detected failure during the execution of the query. If retries is not specified, the global variable mysql-query_retries_on_failure applies.

options.name: rule_id
options.description: The unique id of the rule. Rules are processed in rule_id order.

options.name: save_to_disk
options.description: Save config to sqlite db on disk to persist the configuration.

options.name: schemaname
options.description: Filtering criteria matching schemaname. If I(schemaname) is non-NULL, a query will match only if the connection uses schemaname as its default schema.

options.name: state
options.description: When C(present) - adds the rule, when C(absent) - removes the rule.

options.name: timeout
options.description: The maximum timeout in milliseconds with which the matched or rewritten query should be executed. If a query run for longer than the specific threshold, the query is automatically killed. If timeout is not specified, the global variable mysql-default_query_timeout applies.

options.name: username
options.description: Filtering criteria matching username.  If I(username) is non-NULL, a query will match only if the connection is made with the correct username.
